# Case `V03_trending`

**Category:** input-variability (What the incoming stream looked like)
**Source:** synthetic · **Split:** holdout

## Why it is in the matrix

A linear grade drift across the shift on top of the correlated field. The mean moves, so variance reduction on the whole record becomes a misleading summary of what the plant sees.

## Expected behaviour

VRR may look acceptable while the reclaimed mean drifts; the drift must be visible on the stream plot

## Kill criterion

> If the reclaimed mean does not drift with the input, the trend is not being generated

This is the statement that turns the case from a demonstration into a test. It says, in advance, what
result would mean the code is wrong, and the release gate fails the bake when it is violated.

## Configuration

| parameter | value | what it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `stacking` | `chevron` | the deposition path over the pad |
| `reclaim` | `fullface` | which cells the machine engages and how deep it reaches |
| `n_passes` | 24 | stacker passes, that is layers: the N of the 1/N bound |
| `sr` | 1.0 | the Gray-Thornton segregation number; 0 is a passive tracer |
| `repose_deg` | 37.0 | the imposed angle of repose of the fine species |
| `repose_coarse_deg` | 37.0 | the coarse species; a positive difference is Makse |
| `structure` | `trending` | the autocorrelation structure of the incoming stream |
| `range_t` | 4000 t | the practical range of the input variogram, in tonnes |
| `n_dumps` | 320 | truck loads in the build |
| `reclaim_rate` | 1.0 | tonnes reclaimed per tonne stacked |
| `cut_tonnes` | 900 t | the parcel size the plant receives |
| pad | 64 x 24 cells at 3.0 m | 192 by 72 metres |

## Reproduce it

```bash
python data-pipeline/run.py V03_trending --output build/check --band-seeds 5
```

Omit `--output` only for an intentional canonical release bake. Everything about this case is a pure
function of its parameters and the seed, so two runs produce a byte-identical trace.
